# Decision Record

Why Danny is shaped the way it is. Read this before reopening a settled
question. Format: decision, date, status, reasoning, what would change it.
Superseded decisions are marked, not deleted.

---

## ADR-001 — Native SwiftUI app, project generated by XcodeGen

**2026-09 · Accepted**

A download manager lives in the menu bar and the background for hours; native
SwiftUI gives the lowest resource use and the macOS look the product depends
on. `project.yml` is the source of truth and the `.xcodeproj` is generated, so
project changes review as small YAML diffs and never merge-conflict.

## ADR-002 — macOS 26 only

**2026-09-27 · Accepted**

Liquid Glass is the design, and it only exists on macOS 26. Supporting older
systems meant a second, uglier look behind `#available` checks in every glass
view — code to maintain for users the design doesn't serve. A new app can pick
its baseline.

**Would change it:** a large share of users asking for macOS 15.

## ADR-003 — yt-dlp runs as a child process, not a library

**2026-09 · Accepted**

yt-dlp is Python and changes weekly as sites change. Running it as an
executable keeps Python out of the app, lets it update independently, and
contains its crashes. Danny talks to it through its CLI and a progress template.

## ADR-004 — Plugins run out of process and speak JSON over stdio

**2026-09-27 · Accepted · designed in M2**

Extractors and engines are separate executables that Danny launches and talks
to with JSON messages over stdin/stdout — the same way it already drives yt-dlp.

- **Any language** — Python, Go, Rust, Swift, JS; contributors don't need Xcode.
- **Isolation** — a plugin crash or hang can't take the app down; it can be killed.
- **No code-signing traps** — loading third-party code into a hardened, signed
  app requires disabling library validation; separate processes don't.
- **Any license** — a plugin can be open or closed source; the protocol is the contract.

Rejected: in-process bundles (signing, crashes), JavaScriptCore scripts (can't
do what yt-dlp does), XPC services (macOS-only tooling for contributors).

## ADR-005 — libmpv for playback

**2026-09-27 · Accepted · lands in M3**

Streamed torrents are mostly MKV with HEVC/AV1 and multiple audio/subtitle
tracks. AVPlayer can't open MKV at all. libmpv (via MPVKit) plays everything,
renders with Metal, and costs roughly 20 MB of app size — worth it for a
streaming feature that otherwise fails on most files.

## ADR-006 — Torrent engine as a helper process

**2026-09-27 · Open — decided by an M3 spike**

Same boundary as plugins (ADR-004). Candidates: **librqbit** (Rust, has an HTTP
streaming server built in) and **anacrolix/torrent** (Go, mature streaming
reader). The spike measures memory, CPU while seeding/idle, and time-to-first-frame.

## ADR-007 — `development` → `main`, squash in, merge out

**2026-09-27 · Accepted**

Feature PRs squash into `development` (the PR title becomes the commit and the
changelog line); releases go `development` → `main` with a merge commit so the
tag sits on the released commit. Nobody pushes to either branch directly.

## ADR-008 — Resource use is a feature

**2026-09-27 · Accepted**

Idle Danny costs 0% CPU; downloading costs low single digits. No always-on
timers or animations, effects drawn by Metal shaders, updates throttled, work
stopped when the window is hidden. Changes that add animation or background
work measure it. Rules: [engineering.md](engineering.md) §Danny is light.

## ADR-009 — Clean as you go

**2026-09-27 · Accepted**

The first version was built fast. Rather than a rewrite, every PR leaves what it
touches cleaner, and larger debt is recorded in [backlog.md](backlog.md) and paid
down as its own PRs. The M2 core split is the one planned structural change.

## ADR-010 — Ship outside the App Store: Developer ID + notarization, no sandbox

**2026-09-27 · Accepted**

Danny runs child processes it didn't build (yt-dlp, ffmpeg, plugins — ADR-003/004),
updates yt-dlp on its own schedule, and saves wherever the user points it. The App
Sandbox forbids or cripples all three, so the Mac App Store is out. Distribution is
a DMG and zip on GitHub Releases, signed with a Developer ID, hardened runtime,
notarized and stapled — what Gatekeeper expects from apps outside the store.

Builds made without signing credentials are ad-hoc signed and not notarized, and
their release notes say so. Signed, notarized releases are required before 1.0.

## ADR-011 — Homebrew: our own tap first, the official cask once notarized

**2026-09-27 · Accepted**

`brew install --cask` is how many Mac developers install apps. The official
`homebrew/cask` repo requires apps that pass Gatekeeper and projects notable enough
to meet its criteria, so Danny starts in `orpheus-ui/homebrew-tap` (bumped by the
release workflow) and moves to `homebrew/cask` once both hold. docs/releasing.md.

## ADR-012 — Bundled tools are pinned, verified and native

**2026-09-27 · Accepted**

Releases bundle yt-dlp and ffmpeg so Danny works without Homebrew. Both are
pinned to exact versions and checksum-verified before bundling
(`scripts/fetch-dependencies.sh`), so a release contains exactly what was reviewed
and a compromised download fails the build. ffmpeg is a universal binary built
from native arm64 and x86_64 builds — no Rosetta dependency, which Apple is
phasing out. Bumps are their own PRs.
